One-line judgment: a chiropractor is not a wellness service that just cracks your back, but a diagnostic and treatment occupation that assesses and manages spinal and musculoskeletal problems by manual means within the scope of practice; it requires long periods of close contact with patients, independent clinical judgment and reviewable case notes.

Signals to keep exploring: you can accept long periods of standing and repeated manual force, and you are willing to take a careful history and examine the patient patiently and write your findings and judgments into notes someone else can take over; the O*NET work context shows that 89% have close contact with patients every day, 88% make decisions every day and 40% stand more than half of the time. If you only want to give advice without taking on manual treatment and follow-up responsibility, the gap will be large.

Conditions for pausing before a large investment: you have not yet observed a full consultation and manual treatment in a real clinic, and you have not confirmed whether you can complete a Doctor of Chiropractic programme of about 4 years (usually with at least 3 years of undergraduate study in addition) and pass the state licensing examination. In the United States every state requires a licence to practise; education, examination and licence are three things to be checked separately.

Education, qualifications and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Five (extensive preparation), SVP range 8.0 and above; the education distribution shows 82% of respondents consider a doctoral degree necessary and 8% a professional degree; in the United States you must also complete an accredited programme and pass the NBCE
examinations accepted or required by the state licensing authority, with the scope differing by state. Corresponding diagnostic and treatment activities in mainland China require obtaining the applicable physician qualification and registering by place, category and scope.

In one line: this is an occupation where whether the judgment has a basis, whether contraindications have been excluded, whether the records can be taken over by someone else and whether referral was timely matter more than whether the technique looks elegant; if you are willing to link assessment, treatment and reassessment into a closed loop for each patient, it is worth serious consideration.

The work of a chiropractor can be divided into three connected but distinct work dimensions. The first is assessment and differential diagnosis: take a history and record it, compare range of motion and tenderness on both sides by hand and eye, read or arrange X
rays and other tests when necessary, identify clues to serious causes such as fracture, infection or tumour plus contraindications to manual treatment, and identify red flags requiring referral. The second is manual treatment and supportive plans: choose manual adjustment and other physical means according to the patient's condition, advise on posture and activity and exercise, and use supports such as braces and bandages when necessary. The third is records and follow-up: maintain accurate, reviewable case notes, record responses and reassess, and collaborate with professionals such as family physicians and physiotherapists.
Take a history and examine the patient, identify risks and referral needs, and form a reasoned clinical judgment

Take the history and examine the patient within the lawful scope of practice or training, identify emergencies, contraindications and uncertain items, check tests and imaging as clinically needed and authorized, and form a preliminary judgment and the boundaries of the plan with truthful records. The structure is editorial and not a clinical treatment guideline; a suspected emergency does not wait for all the steps to be completed. The NHS2026 UK back pain material lists back pain with pain, numbness or weakness in both legs, loss of perineal sensation and new changes in bladder or bowel function as emergency warning signs. When an emergency is suspected, routine manual treatment should stop and the local emergency care pathway should be followed, without waiting for AI prompts, routine reassessment or completion of an internal checklist; this is not a list that excludes all serious causes.
Develop and carry out the manual adjustment and supportive plan

Agree the treatment goals and frequency with the patient, choose manual adjustment and other physical means and explain the risks and alternatives, carry it out on site and observe the patient's response and tolerance, arrange supports such as braces and bandages and home exercises, record this session's treatment and immediate response, and agree the reassessment time point and the situations in which to make contact earlier

Maintain accurate case notes recording the patient's statements, the actual examination and treatment, responses, reassessment and referrals; do not make out-of-scope efficacy promises to third parties, but do not conceal communication or events that have already occurred in the notes. Article 24 of China's Physicians Law prohibits concealing, forging or altering case notes, or destroying them without authorization.

Physiotherapy focuses on functional recovery and may also use manual techniques; acupuncture uses needle insertion at acupoints as its main task; massage therapy addresses soft tissue and joints and may also assist with range of motion and muscle strength assessment and propose a service plan. Family medicine covers diagnosis and treatment across the life course and prevention; sports medicine focuses on sports-related injuries. Tasks can overlap, but the licence to practise and responsibility depend on the specific jurisdiction and cannot be exchanged by title.
The two share some patients, but the core technique differs: this occupation uses manual adjustment of the spine and joints as its signature technique and bears treatment responsibility for it
Physiotherapists mainly use exercise and physical means, focusing on functional rehabilitation and recovery of movement capacity

The U.S. occupational description focuses on the neuromuscular skeletal system, uses history and examination and imaging as the basis, and uses chiropractic diagnostic systems to assess function (manual adjustment task importance 100, obtaining and recording patient histories 96), referring out when beyond scope
Family medicine physicians do general diagnosis and medication and chronic disease management, covering the whole body

The closed loop of this occupation is taking the history, examination and differential diagnosis, identifying referral or testing needs, developing and carrying out the manual or supportive plan, recording responses and reassessing
Acupuncturists mainly use needling and traditional Chinese medicine pattern differentiation, treating according to meridian and pattern concepts

The outputs of this occupation are reviewable case notes and imaging interpretation records, treatment and reassessment records, referral and collaboration records and patient education materials, and it is responsible for treatment outcomes

Massage therapy addresses soft tissue and joints and may also assist with range of motion and muscle strength assessment or propose a service plan; it should not be misdescribed as a relaxation service with no treatment plan or responsibility.

Compared with the other directions, this occupation carries responsibility for diagnostic and treatment decisions; within an institution there are also professionals responsible for tests and imaging and referral

Diagnostic and treatment decisions are made by a qualified chiropractor, and what this page presents are the boundaries of tasks and outputs and do not constitute any practice or statutory distribution of duties

U.S. OOH: a D.C. must come from an accredited chiropractic college, usually 4 years, with at least 3 years of undergraduate study before applying and with prerequisite courses checked; all states require a licence, and the specific examinations, background checks and state law examination conditions are checked state by state. NBCE currently states that 50 states accept or require Examinations I—IV, and passing the examinations is not itself a licence; continuing education is also required to practise.

Articles 11, 13 and 14 of China's Physicians Law set out qualification assessment and examination, practice registration and the place, category and scope of registration respectively; an overseas D.C. or a short training certificate cannot be converted directly into practice authority in China. The traditional Chinese medicine specialty pathway obtains a qualification through assessment and practises within the registered scope; this round does not replace individual application, registration or determination of technical authorization.
The conclusion applies only to the O*NET and BLS bases and periods stated on this page and does not constitute a judgment about scope of practice or exchange of qualifications

Comparing positions cannot rely on similar titles alone; diagnostic authorization, the core intervention, referral responsibility and legal risk differ, and similar tasks do not mean the positions can be exchanged

Six editorial self-checks: whether emergencies and referral needs are identified; whether individual risk and contraindications are assessed; whether the records can be taken over; whether tests and imaging are necessary and authorized; whether goals, risks, alternatives and reassessment are communicated; and whether the work is within the lawful scope of practice and competence. A checklist cannot prove that all risks have been excluded.
Judgment one: whether emergencies and referral needs are identified

The NHS2026 UK back pain material lists back pain with pain, numbness or weakness in both legs, loss of perineal sensation and new changes in bladder or bowel function as emergency warning signs. When an emergency is suspected, routine manual treatment should stop and the local emergency care pathway should be followed, without waiting for AI prompts, routine reassessment or completion of an internal checklist; this is not a list that excludes all serious causes.
Judgment two: whether contraindications and risks of manual treatment are assessed

NCCIH notes that manual treatment may cause transient pain, discomfort, stiffness or headache; serious spinal, neurological or cervical artery related events have been reported, but accurate incidence rates are lacking. The causal link between cervical manipulation and arterial dissection remains disputed, and the potential risk must be explained. Health status, medication, the specific technique and the site must be assessed case by case by a qualified person; osteoporosis, anticoagulation or trauma cannot all be written as the same contraindication for all manual techniques, nor can this page's checklist be used to conclude that treatment is permissible.
Judgment three: whether the treatment and records can be taken over by someone else

The case notes should record the presenting complaint, findings, basis, treatment, response and follow-up; conclusions without a basis increase the difficulty of review and continuity of care, and facts that have occurred must not be deleted or a basis fabricated afterwards.
Judgment four: whether tests and imaging are necessary

Check the actual clinical need for imaging, the question being asked and the operating authorization, and do not make radiography a routine item for all patients; Article 31 of China's Physicians Law prohibits unnecessary examination and treatment. Protection and explanation follow the applicable standards, and an occupational task list cannot grant imaging operating rights.
Judgment five: whether the course of treatment and the expectations are made clear

Whether the course, frequency, expected improvement and stopping conditions are explained to the patient, avoiding indefinite maintenance treatment; when expectations are not met, reassess and consider referral rather than simply extending the same plan.
Judgment six: whether the work is within the boundaries of authorization and competence

Whether practice is within the licence and the institution's authorization, without promising to cure diseases outside that scope; advertising and promises beyond the scope should be refused, and the boundaries that were explained should be recorded truthfully in the case notes.

Chiropractors assess, treat and care for patients by manually adjusting the spine and musculoskeletal system, and may also perform spinal adjustments or address misalignment of the sacroiliac joint and pelvis; the work is mainly outpatient consultations, with a typical closed loop of taking the history, assessing the neuromuscular skeletal state, identifying referral or testing needs, developing and carrying out the manual or supportive plan, and recording responses and reassessing.

The current 2026 O*NET29-1011.00 occupational definition is assessing, treating and caring for spinal and musculoskeletal problems, with tasks including manual adjustment, history taking, judgment, records and referral; Job Zone
Five and SVP8.0 and above. The current O*NET six interest importance ratings are R76 tied with S76, and I63/C43/E19/A6; the top three specific areas are medical services 90, social service 46 and medical science 45. They describe occupational task interests, not the proportions of practitioners, an individual type distribution or a hiring threshold.

U.S. wages on the BLS OEWS May 2025 basis (shown on the O*NET page for this occupation, 29-1011.00): the 10/25/50/75/90 annual percentiles are 43,460, 60,070, 79,200, 105,050 and 146,080 USD; the 10/25/50/75/90 hourly percentiles are 20.90,
28.88, 38.08, 50.51 and 70.23 USD. The percentiles describe positions in the distribution of employed wage and salary positions and exclude the self-employed and owners or partners of unincorporated businesses; this cannot be used to exclude wages received by owners of all incorporated practices.

NBS2025 urban unit health and social work category: non-private annual average 146,266 yuan, private 75,631 yuan. If the actual employer falls in that category this can serve as industry background; it includes other positions, and the non-private and private populations differ, so it is not the national wage, monthly wage, starting salary or a percentile for chiropractors. The self-employed and freelancers are not in the urban unit sample; the actual legal entity's industry classification must be checked. The precise national and regional wage for this occupation in China remains insufficient evidence.

BLS U.S. SOC29-1011: 2025 employment 61,700 to a 2035 projection of 67,000, a net gain of 5,300, a whole-number growth of 9%, and 2,600 openings per year on average, including replacement needs from people moving to other occupations or leaving the labour force. Employment includes 36% self-employed in 2025, while the wage sample excludes the self-employed and owners or partners of unincorporated businesses; a projection is not the current hiring volume, year-by-year actual performance or AI causality. The current O*NET industry distribution is health
and social assistance 63% and other 37%; OOH separately lists chiropractic clinics 57% and self-employed 36%, and the two sets of classifications are not the same basis.

O*NET lists 8 software categories: billing, scheduling, email, ERP, medical, office, spreadsheet and word processing; the separate hot technology list contains only 4 items, and in 2025 U.S. deduplicated postings Office and Excel are below 1% with no percentage provided for Outlook and Word. entries: Manual treatment｜Perform manual adjustment on the spine and other joints｜Perform a series of manual adjustments on the spinal column or other joints to correct the musculoskeletal system, and address sacroiliac joint and pelvic misalignment (corresponding to O*NET task importance 100).

Assessment and differential diagnosis｜Take a history and examine the patient and assess the neuromuscular skeletal state｜Obtain and record patient histories, diagnose health problems by reviewing histories and questioning and observing and examining patients and reading X-rays, and use chiropractic diagnostic systems to assess the function of the neuromuscular skeletal system and spine (corresponding to task importance 96, 96 and 94).

Tests and imaging｜Arrange and interpret tests and imaging according to indications｜Take X-rays and analyse images to locate the source of problems and exclude fracture or disease, and recommend and arrange diagnostic procedures such as blood chemistry and saliva and other imaging (corresponding to task importance: analysing images 82, taking radiographs 78, arranging tests 78).

Case notes and records｜Maintain accurate, reviewable patient case notes｜Maintain accurate and complete patient history records, and write each treatment and response and reassessment into the notes (corresponding to task importance 94).

Patient education and support｜Explain the plan and advise on exercise and supports｜Advise patients on treatment plans, counsel them on nutrition and exercise and sleep and stress management, instruct patients in exercises to improve range of motion, and use supports such as strapping and taping and bandages or braces when needed (corresponding to task importance: treatment plans 89, lifestyle counselling 87, exercise 86, supportive devices 70).

Referral and collaboration｜Refer out when beyond scope and collaborate with other professionals｜Consult with or refer patients to other suitable health practitioners when necessary, and support subsequent collaboration and reassessment with clear, checkable case notes (corresponding to task importance 90).

paragraphs:
Workplace and posture｜97% work indoors in a controlled environment every day; 40% stand more than half of the time; 32% bend or twist more than half of the time; 36% continuously or almost continuously use their hands to grasp or manipulate and feel objects and tools.
Contact with people｜89% answer that the job requires being very close to others (nearly physical contact), which is not a daily frequency; 89% have face-to-face discussions every day; 74% have ongoing contact with others; 85%
consider dealing directly with external customers or the public extremely important.
Decisions and autonomy｜99% have a great deal of freedom in setting tasks and priorities and goals; 88% have a great deal of freedom in decisions; 88% make decisions every day; 21% consider the consequences of an error very serious.
Communication methods and tools｜70% use email every day; 49% have telephone conversations every day; 38% write letters and memos at least weekly but not daily; 36%
consider coordinating or leading others at work extremely important.
Time and pace｜50% of respondents have a typical work week above 40 hours; 34% feel time pressure every day; 46% consider repeating the same tasks very important; 53% consider the level of competition high.
Results and responsibility｜68% consider the effect of decisions on colleagues or the institution very important; 37%
have very high responsibility for the work results of others; 18% have high responsibility for the health and safety of other workers.
Emotion and conflict｜19% encounter conflict situations at least weekly but not daily; outpatient work has to handle the emotional responses brought by pain and anxiety, and complaints and boundary problems should be recorded.
Physical load｜Manual treatment requires continuous manual force and repeated bending and turning, and the work is mainly standing and working in close-range positions, so breaks and self-protection must be arranged.
Qualification and responsibility boundaries｜Every U.S. state requires a licence to practise; diagnostic and treatment decisions are made by qualified personnel, and matters beyond the scope of practice must be referred and recorded. The context percentages are U.S. respondent answers, not a share of patient safety responsibility or an incident probability; physical load management is editorial advice.

The six directions share some capabilities with this occupation: history taking and examination, manual assessment and treatment, patient communication, and awareness of records and referral. The real differences lie in the qualification (whether there is diagnostic and prescribing or practice authorization), the means (manual and exercise, or needling and medication) and the responsibility (whether the person is answerable for diagnostic and treatment outcomes). When choosing, it is better to test with one deliverable assessment and plan than to compare titles.

The basis for comparison is the task and work activity descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 29-1011.00 page, the adjacent occupation notes registered in this evidence route, and the public occupational materials for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial compilation and does not constitute a conclusion about scope of practice or exchange of qualifications.

The table below compares positions and occupations adjacent to this occupation: physical therapists, acupuncturists, massage therapists, family medicine physicians, sports medicine physicians and nurse practitioners. The four columns each answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Physical therapists mainly use exercise and physical means other than manual techniques and focus on functional rehabilitation; this occupation uses manual adjustment of the spine and joints as its signature technique, the two share some patients, but the means, authorization and referral relationship differ.

People who want to do long-term assessment and functional training plans in a clinic are suited to the physiotherapy direction; people willing to use spinal and joint manual techniques as the main means are suited to this occupation.
Assess and treat movement function problems with exercise and physical means, with outputs mainly functional assessment and training plans and progress records.
Physical therapists

Acupuncturists use needling and traditional Chinese medicine theory as their means and need the corresponding practice qualification; this occupation focuses on manual adjustment and neuromuscular skeletal assessment, both address pain but the theoretical framework and regulatory system differ.

People who want to manage pain within the traditional Chinese medicine theoretical system are suited to the acupuncture direction; people who want to do manual assessment based on anatomy and biomechanics are suited to this occupation.

Carry out needling and other treatment according to traditional Chinese medicine theory and meridian pattern differentiation, with outputs mainly pattern differentiation records and prescriptions and course records.
Acupuncturists

Massage therapists mainly use soft tissue work and relaxation techniques and usually do not carry diagnostic and treatment decisions; this occupation carries diagnostic and treatment decisions and is answerable for outcomes.

People who want to work mainly with their hands but not carry diagnostic responsibility are suited to the massage therapy direction; people willing to make independent clinical judgments and bear responsibility for outcomes are suited to this occupation.
Relieve muscle tension with soft tissue and relaxation techniques, with outputs mainly service records and client feedback.
Massage therapists

Family medicine physicians carry general diagnostic and medication and prescribing authority; this occupation focuses only on the neuromuscular skeletal system and must refer out when beyond scope, and the two are not the same level of practice authorization.

People who want to do general diagnosis and treatment and chronic disease management are suited to the family medicine direction; people who want to focus on spinal and musculoskeletal problems are suited to this occupation.
Diagnose and treat common diseases from a general practice perspective and manage chronic disease, with outputs mainly diagnosis and medication and follow-up records.
Family medicine physicians

Sports medicine physicians have authority for diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries and for surgery or injection; this occupation focuses on manual assessment and conservative treatment, and situations needing surgery or imaging interpretation must be referred out.

People who want to handle the whole pathway of competitive and sports injuries are suited to the sports medicine direction; people who want outpatient manual treatment and conservative rehabilitation are suited to this occupation.
Diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries and return-to-training form the main line, with outputs mainly diagnosis and treatment and return-to-training plans and follow-up records.
Sports medicine physicians

Nurse practitioners have prescribing and partial diagnostic and treatment authority and work within a team; this occupation practises independently and carries diagnostic and treatment decisions, and the entry pathways and scopes of authority in the United States are entirely different.

People who want to do continuous care and medication management within a health care team are suited to the nursing direction; people who want independent outpatient practice and responsibility for manual treatment are suited to this occupation.
Focus on continuous patient care and medication and health management, with outputs mainly nursing assessments and prescriptions and follow-up records.
Nurse practitioners

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually requires filling in new qualifications and tools: the physiotherapy and nurse practitioner directions need different education and licences, the acupuncturist and massage therapist directions need their own practice qualifications, and the family medicine and sports medicine directions need a medical degree and residency training. History taking and patient communication and record keeping are transferable, but the scope of authorization must be re-checked item by item.

paragraphs: Students and career changers preparing to enter the occupation

First build solid fundamentals in history taking and examination, red flag and contraindication identification, case note keeping and manual technique, then learn to use electronic records and clinic management software to organize and retrieve information; do not replace systematic training with technique demonstrations in short videos, as safety and scope of practice are the bottom line of this occupation.
Practitioners who perform manual treatment in an outpatient setting

Use documentation and retrieval tools for organizing case notes and patient education and follow-up reminders, but keep contraindication judgments, imaging interpretation, treatment decisions and referral within your own professional judgment and review.
Positions responsible for case note quality and outpatient processes

Use templates and checklists to improve note completeness and follow-up visibility, but write the determination and reassessment of red flags and contraindications clearly, and avoid letting system prompts replace clinical reasoning.

entries.answer:
Daily tasks are mainly consultations and examinations and manual treatment and records: performing manual adjustment on the spine and other joints, obtaining and recording patient histories, diagnosing through history taking and observation and examination and reading X-rays, using chiropractic diagnostic systems to assess neuromuscular skeletal and spinal function, maintaining accurate and complete case notes, counselling on nutrition and exercise and sleep and stress management, and consulting with or referring to other health practitioners when necessary. The O*NET work context shows that 89%
have close contact with patients every day, 88% make decisions every day and 40% stand more than half of the time.
entries.question: What do chiropractors do every day?

entries.answer: Compared with physical therapists, this occupation uses manual adjustment of the spine and joints as its signature technique; compared with acupuncturists, the theoretical framework and practice system differ; compared with massage therapists, this occupation carries diagnostic and treatment decisions and is answerable for outcomes; compared with family medicine physicians, this occupation focuses only on the neuromuscular skeletal system and must refer out when beyond scope. Sharing some patients does not mean the positions can be exchanged: diagnostic authorization, the core intervention and referral responsibility all differ.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between chiropractors and adjacent occupations?

entries.answer: That cannot be inferred. The core tasks of this occupation are mainly manual assessment and treatment, red flag and contraindication identification, and patient communication and records; judging tissue and joint condition by hand, identifying situations in which manual treatment must not be performed, and bearing responsibility for treatment outcomes all require long training and personal practice responsibility; AI output can neither replace a licence nor exempt the duty to inform and record.
entries.question: Will AI replace chiropractors?

entries.answer: The earlier affected parts are those that can be structured as inputs: organizing case notes and documents and generating summaries, follow-up and reassessment reminders, information retrieval and checking insurance and pricing. The later affected parts are those that must be done by hand on site and carry responsibility: examination and manual adjustment, and contraindication and red flag judgments and referral decisions.
entries.question: Which chiropractor tasks are most easily automated?

entries.answer: Making clinical judgments by hand, holding a position between patient expectations and safety boundaries, integrating examination and imaging and history into a reviewable conclusion, and deciding to refer when information is insufficient. These abilities depend on long training and personal practice responsibility, not on tool proficiency.
entries.question: Which abilities are hard for AI to replace?

entries.answer: In the United States a Doctor of Chiropractic degree is usually required, and completing the programme usually takes about 4 years, with at least 3 years of undergraduate study in addition; the education distribution on the O*NET page for this occupation is doctorate 82%, professional degree 8% and post-high-school certificate 7%. entries.question: What education do you need to become a chiropractor?

entries.answer: In the United States every state requires a licence to practise, and the common pathway is completing an accredited programme and passing the NBCE examinations accepted or required by the state licensing authority; the specific requirements differ by state. Professional association certification (such as in the sports chiropractic and neurological chiropractic directions) is proof of ability and direction, not the same as a licence. In mainland China the corresponding diagnostic and treatment activities require completing physician qualification and practice registration by place and category and scope.
entries.question: Which licences or certifications are needed?

entries.answer: It requires investing again along the education and licensing pathway: usually completing undergraduate prerequisite courses, then about 4 years of a degree programme and passing the state examination. If you already have a health or sports background, anatomy and physiology and communication and record-keeping experience transfer partly, but the licence and scope of practice must be obtained anew, and a position cannot be taken by title alone.
entries.question: Is it realistic to change careers into chiropractic?

entries.answer: It depends on whether you are willing to make clinical judgments by hand over the long term and bear responsibility for outcomes, and whether you can accept a relatively large investment in education and licensing. BLS projects employment growth of 9% over 2025 to 2035 (much faster than the average for all occupations) with about 2,600 openings per year on average, but self-employment is relatively common in this occupation and income structures vary widely. It is advisable to first use the seven-day exercise on the page to test whether you would want to repeat this process.

description.text: Chiropractors assess and manage spinal and musculoskeletal problems by manual means, with history taking and examination, manual treatment, imaging and test judgment, and case notes and follow-up at the core: tasks and work context, the U.S. BLS wage and employment basis, mainland China statistical gaps, and entry and practice qualification paths, risks and exercises all in one view.

subject.name: Chiropractors
subject.summary: Assess, treat and care for patients by manually adjusting the spine and musculoskeletal system: take the history and examine the patient, identify red flags and manual treatment contraindications, arrange tests and imaging by indication, develop and carry out the manual or supportive plan, record responses and reassess, and refer out when beyond the scope of practice.
